acceptance.check: Members screen shows the group's invite link with Copy link as the primary action; rotate/disable controls render only for the owner and are absent for a plain member.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Sign in as owner and as member; assert invite URL contains the token and Copy confirms in place; assert controls absent for member.

acceptance.check: Opening the invite link as a signed-in non-member via the confirm action creates exactly one membership and lands on the group overview; confirming again leaves one active membership row; concurrent double-open yields one row.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Integration test confirms twice plus concurrent opens, asserts one active member row and second call is a no-op; QA repeats in browser and lands on overview.

acceptance.check: After rotation the old token 404s and the new token joins; after disable the token 404s; a signed-out GET on a valid token redirects to /sign-in and carries the join destination.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Integration test for rotate/disabled/invalid token states; QA drives signed-out open and asserts redirect.

acceptance.check: Owner adds a placeholder by name (trimmed, 1-80 chars); the name appears in the member list and member pickers marked as placeholder with a Claim action.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Call add-placeholder action, assert members list contains the name with placeholder marker and Claim control; component test asserts picker includes it.

acceptance.check: Claiming a placeholder as a signed-in user attaches their user_id to that member row so prior rows read as theirs; claiming an already-claimed placeholder is refused with an already-claimed message; a removed placeholder reports no-longer-available, not already-claimed.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Integration test claims then re-claims as a second user and asserts refusal and unchanged row; claims a removed placeholder and asserts the distinct message; QA claims in browser.

acceptance.check: Two concurrent claims on the same placeholder produce exactly one winner: one succeeds, the other is told it is already claimed, and only one user_id is stored; a claimer who already holds an active membership is refused without a 500.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Integration test firing two concurrent claim transactions against one placeholder asserts one success and one conflict; member-then-claim test asserts refusal.

acceptance.check: Join, placeholder add, claim, rotate and disable each write exactly one activity entry naming the actor in the same transaction as the change; a failed feed write rolls the change back.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Integration test asserts one entry per mutation with actor and member linkage, and feed-mock failure leaves rows unchanged.

acceptance.check: Invite block renders a static skeleton while loading (token never flashes as missing) and the copy action confirms in place with a fallback when clipboard is unavailable.
acceptance.how_to_verify: QA throttles load, asserts skeleton shape then link; clicks Copy and asserts in-place confirmation text.

acceptance.check: Invite join is idempotent, rotation immediately invalidates the previous token, and disable rejects the token (TR-14); the join GET is write-free so prefetch/crawler fetches never create memberships.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Integration test: double-open yields one membership; rotate rejects old and accepts new; disable rejects; GET-only fetch creates no row.

acceptance.check: Placeholder claim is atomic with no shared history and prior records belong to the claimer (TR-15); claimed rows resolve the live profile name, placeholders resolve the stored name.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Concurrent-claim integration test plus assertion that the winner owns the member row and readMembers coalesces members.display_name ?? users.display_name.

alternatives_considered.approach: Separate invite_tokens table with one row per rotation instead of invite_token/invite_enabled columns on groups.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The product needs exactly one live token per group with immediate invalidation; a history table adds a second source for which token works and a join on every open, for audit value nothing reads.

alternatives_considered.approach: Claim by inserting a new member row for the claimer and repointing expense_payer/expense_share rows to it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Repointing rewrites ledger history and risks partial moves; attaching user_id to the same row reattributes everything by construction with one UPDATE, which is also what makes the race a single-row atomic write.

alternatives_considered.approach: Join via a POST-only Server Action with no GET route.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: IAC-2/IAC-3 require a screen the link opens that a signed-out person can open and be redirected from; a form-only action has no URL to share or paste.

validated_work_order.approach: Build invites/placeholders on the existing invite_token/invite_enabled columns and nullable members.user_id with its partial unique index, fixing the proposal's four load-bearing errors: (1) commit the migration through the journal so it runs; (2) make join and claim single-statement atomic writes with NOT EXISTS guards so idempotence and the already-a-member refusal never 500; (3) keep GET /join/[token] write-free with a confirm POST so prefetch never joins and the action owns revalidatePath; (4) store display_name only for placeholders and coalesce with the live profile name so TR-12 renames never go stale. All writes stay in src/lib/access.ts called by Zod-validated Server Actions in one transaction with exactly one recordActivity; invite-rotation kinds are excluded from the overview recent feed so the empty state survives; component fixtures are updated with the new required fields. No money code touched per the binding keep-everything-else decision.
assumptions: The join URL shape /join/[token] is free to choose; no existing link format or test pins it.
New activity kinds are acceptable additions; activity.kind is free text with no DB check constraint.
A caller who is already an active member may not claim a placeholder (refused); claiming is how a non-member becomes one.
Claim keeps the placeholder stored name for the placeholder row only; claimed rows resolve the live profile name.
Balance precondition from piece 2 does not yet exist as code, so this plan does not enforce it on remove/leave paths.
validated_work_order.confidence_rationale: Code paths mapped to real functions and callers (migrate.ts journal gating, partial unique index, GROUP_LIFECYCLE_KINDS exclusion, Record describe, layout requireUser, profile rename path); the only new DB surface is one nullable column plus app-level kinds. Points off for the open activity-kind naming choice, untested archived-group and rotate-then-disable interactions, and PGlite-vs-Neon concurrency fidelity on the race test.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: Accepted all nine critique findings after re-checking each against the code: the missing journal entry, the claim 500 when the claimer is already a member, the read-then-insert join race, the GET-that-writes with a dead revalidatePath, the stale-name backfill, the two component fixtures that fail tsc, the invite kinds displacing the empty state, the removed-vs-claimed message conflation, and the missing placeholder-name validation. No finding contradicts the binding brief decision (money core untouched).

Repo has invite columns, nullable user_id with partial unique index, activity-in-transaction pattern; missing join route, rotate/disable/add/claim writes, placeholder name, invite UI.
